questions.q: What is the key insight that lets DPO avoid training a separate reward model?
options: DPO simply ignores preference data entirely

Under a KL-constrained reward-maximization objective, the optimal policy and the reward function are related by a closed form, so that relationship can be substituted directly into the preference loss
DPO uses a much larger reward model instead of a smaller one
DPO trains the reward model and the policy simultaneously in the same network with no connection between them
questions.explain: DPO reparameterizes the Bradley-Terry loss using the closed-form relationship between the KL-constrained optimal policy and its implied reward, eliminating the need to learn a separate reward function first.

options: As the output of a separately trained scalar reward network
As beta times the log-ratio of the policy's probability to the reference model's probability for a given response
As a fixed constant set before training begins
As the number of tokens in the generated response
questions.explain: The implicit reward is r(x,y) = beta * log(pi_theta(y|x) / pi_ref(y|x)) — defined entirely from the policy's own log-probabilities relative to the frozen reference model.

questions.q: What does the DPO loss function do with a (prompt, chosen, rejected) triple?
options: It ignores the rejected response entirely
It increases the policy's relative log-probability (versus the reference model) of the chosen response and decreases it for the rejected response, scaled by a sigmoid term
It trains a classifier to predict which response is longer
It discards the prompt and only compares the two responses to each other directly
questions.explain: DPO's loss is -log sigma(beta * [log-ratio for chosen - log-ratio for rejected]), which pushes up the chosen response's relative likelihood and pushes down the rejected one's.

questions.q: What role does beta play in DPO, and what is its PPO-based RLHF analog?
options: Beta has no analog in PPO-based RLHF
Beta controls how far the policy can move from the reference model to satisfy a preference, playing the same role as the KL coefficient in PPO-based RLHF
Beta is the learning rate used only during the SFT stage
Beta determines the number of PPO rollout steps per batch
questions.explain: Just as PPO's KL coefficient controls how far the policy can drift from the reference model while chasing reward, DPO's beta controls the same tradeoff within its closed-form loss.

questions.q: What kind of dataset does TRL's DPOTrainer expect, and how does it relate to the data used to train a reward model in Chapter 6?
options: A dataset of single responses with no comparisons, entirely different from reward model training data
A dataset with prompt, chosen, and rejected columns — the same shape as the preference pairs used to train a reward model, just consumed by a different loss
A dataset of raw pretraining text with no labels at all
A dataset of PPO rollout trajectories generated during training
questions.explain: DPO trains directly on the same (prompt, chosen, rejected) preference data that would otherwise train a Bradley-Terry reward model — DPO just uses a different, reward-model-free loss on it.
